items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: But years ago I used to play with Muggsy Spanier and I played with Eddie Condon and Bobby Hackett and Jimmy McPartland. That was just little stints, eight weeks here, maybe sixteen weeks there, three weeks there.

ctx.x: And how did you get your start in the world of music?

Well when I was eleven or twelve years old I had a very close friend of my family, his name was Joe Marsala, who was a clarinetist in his own right, he had his own band on 52nd Street, and played with Wingy Manone, played with Louis Prima, played with all of — Bobby Hackett, Eddie Condon, played with all the great bands and he kind of took me under his wing and started giving me clarinet lessons. I asked to have them and it was a good experience because I would go out on location to jobs with him when he used to…
That’s pretty fascinating for a young man.
